claim: State Illinois transfer tax is imposed on the privilege of transferring title to Illinois real estate (also beneficial interests and controlling interests) at 50 cents for each $500 of value or fraction of $500 stated in the declaration; if the transferring document states the transfer is subject to a mortgage, the outstanding mortgage amount is excluded from the tax basis; tax is due whether or not a document is recorded.

Recorder/registrar of titles of the county collects the state tax by selling revenue stamps at 50 cents per $500 or fraction; paper stamps phased out by Dec 31, 2025, after which counties issue electronic revenue stamps or alternative indicia.

A deed cannot be accepted for filing by a recorder unless revenue stamps in the required amount have been purchased from the recorder (except exempt deeds under 31-45); stamps are affixed by the recorder before or after recording at grantee's request.

A transfer declaration, signed by at least one seller and one buyer (or their attorneys/agents), must be presented to the recorder with the deed, or within 3 business days after the transfer is effected, whichever is earlier; the form is prescribed by the Department of Revenue; a deed is not accepted for recordation without it (except as provided in 31-45).

Statutory exemptions from state transfer tax include: deeds to/from governmental bodies and charitable/religious/educational organizations (still must file declaration); deeds securing debt; confirmatory/corrective deeds without added consideration; actual consideration less than $100; tax deeds; deeds releasing security; deeds of partition; deeds in exchange of real estate (money difference taxable); deeds issued to a mortgage holder pursuant to foreclosure or transfer in lieu of foreclosure; certain Home Ownership Made Easy Act purchases (declaration still required).

County board may impose a county transfer tax at 25 cents for each $500 of value or fraction stated in the declaration; collected by recorder before recording; deeds exempt under 35 ILCS 200/31-45 are also exempt; the county tax is in addition to other state/municipal privilege taxes; mortgage outstanding excluded from basis.

IDOR: Form PTAX-203 transfer declaration (and 203-A, 203-B) can be submitted via MyDec; MyDec also accepts City of Chicago Form 7551 Real Property Transfer Tax Declaration and declarations for participating counties; non-MyDec counties use fill-in PDF forms.

Redemption period for residential real estate ends on the later of (i) 7 months from the date all mortgagors were served/submitted to jurisdiction or (ii) 3 months from entry of judgment of foreclosure; for non-residential foreclosures it is the later of 6 months from service or 3 months from judgment.

Redemption period is shortened to the later of the end of any reinstatement period or 60 days after judgment if the court finds the value is under 90% of the redemption amount and the mortgagee waives deficiency; shortened to 30 days after judgment if the property is abandoned.

Owner of redemption must give written notice of intent to redeem to mortgagee's attorney at least 15 days (excluding weekends/court holidays) before the designated redemption date; once expired, the right of redemption is not revived.

Board of review complaint that the assessment is over/under-assessed to affect the current year must be filed within 30 calendar days after the date of publication of the assessment list (Sec. 12-10); mailed complaints are filed as of postmark date; complaints must be in writing; where a change of $100,000+ in assessed valuation is sought, board serves the petition on taxing districts at least 14 days before hearing.

General Homestead Exemption (35 ILCS 200/15-175): reduction equals the increase in current EAV above 1977 EAV, up to a max of $10,000 in Cook County, $8,000 in counties contiguous to Cook, $6,000 in all other counties (per IDOR PIO-74, R-07/25).

Senior Citizens Homestead Exemption (age 65+): max EAV reduction $8,000 in Cook County and contiguous counties, $5,000 in all other counties; Cook County requires annual application to the Cook County Assessor.

Low-income Senior Citizens Assessment Freeze Homestead Exemption (senior freeze): age 65+, household income limit $75,000 or less for taxable year 2026 (payable 2027), $77,000 for 2027, $79,000 for 2028 and after; freezes EAV at base year; Form PTAX-340 filed annually with Chief County Assessment Office.

Other exemptions: Persons with Disabilities $2,000 EAV reduction (15-168); Standard Homestead Exemption for Veterans with Disabilities $2,500/$5,000/first $250,000 EAV by disability percentage (15-169); Returning Veterans $5,000 (15-167); Homestead Improvement Exemption up to $75,000 fair cash value ($25,000 assessed) for 4 years (15-180).

Senior Citizens Real Estate Tax Deferral Program (320 ILCS 30): age 65+, deferral is a loan secured by lien, repaid when property is sold or transferred, within one year of death, or 90 days after property ceases to qualify; max deferral 80% of taxpayer's equity.
